newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - ADRs slump on Greenspan comments.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - ADRs slump on Greenspan comments.

text.p: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) largely eased on Wednesday on comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan that the stock market's rise could be unsustainable.
Decliners led advancers 300 to 171 among 807 ADRs. Volume was 33 million shares in late morning.

Latin American ADRs in particular dropped on Greenspan's semi-annual congressional testimony on the U.S. economy. Latin American stocks are especially sensitive to prices of U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds, which slumped on his comments.

"They all got hit on the Greenspan comment," said Ray Kelly, Latin American director at Robert Fleming. "Today is going to be a trading day." 1-5/8 to 99-3/8 and Telefonos de Mexico fell 5/8 to 40. Volume in both was heavy and the ADRs were among the most active shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Among the gainers, Dutch chemicals group Akzo Nobel rose 1-1/4 to 75-1/4 ahead of the release of 1996 results on Thursday. Analysts expect solid profit growth.

Among Asian ADRs, China's Jilin Chemical Industrial Co rose 5/8 to 13-7/8, boosted by renewed interest from investors following the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping. China Eastern Airlines Corp Ltd rose 1-1/2 to 21-7/8.
